Since the 2024 presidential election, the S&P 500’s total return climbed more than 25% as of April 20, 2026, despite significant volatility along the way.[1](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_c718) “In the wake of the recent conflict and April 2025 trade announcements, investors have overcome concerns about economic growth,” says Bill Merz, head of capital markets research for U.S. Bank Asset Management Group. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act ([OBBBA](https://www.usbank.com/wealth-management/financial-perspectives/financial-planning/the-real-impact-of-the-tax-cuts-and-jobs-act.html)) lowered corporate and individual taxes, and federal tax refunds were running approximately $40 billion higher than in 2025 through April 17.[1](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_f541) Earlier Federal Reserve rate cuts also helped support borrowing and spending, which gave investors another reason to stay constructive. S&P 500 companies increased fourth-quarter 2025 revenue by 9.2% and earnings by 13.4%, while current first-quarter expectations point to revenue growth of 9.6% and earnings growth of 13.0%.[1](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_a7c) Those fundamentals help explain why investors have continued to buy despite higher oil prices and policy noise.
